In the source, the target is the large blue mug left of the headphones; in the edit, that mug appears as a blurred blue remnant on the far left, while two small mugs are visible and one is right of the headphones. This creates a target-identity/binding ambiguity: do not silently count a different or duplicated mug as the requested target. Bind the mug across source and edit using its visual identity, and assess both whether that same mug moved toward the requested position and whether it is now to the right. Keep completion and progress as distinct criteria: a final right-side relation alone does not establish that the original mug was moved, while a demonstrated move that falls short can support partial. Have the node cite the relevant source-to-edit evidence and preserve uncertainty when identity or movement cannot be established; do not infer absence of progress from low confidence. The trace’s high-confidence yes conflicts with the partial aggregate, so ensure the decision criterion resolves that distinction rather than letting supporting observations independently imply completion.
